tagline: Five miles of red road into Zion's back corner.
intro: Off I-15 at Exit 40, seventeen miles south of Cedar City, the Kolob Canyons Road runs into the northwest corner of Zion. It follows a fault line beneath the five finger canyons of Kolob, narrow box canyons cut into 2,000-foot cliffs at the western edge of the Colorado Plateau, and climbs red asphalt switchbacks for more than 1,000 feet in five miles.
Mormon settlers named the country Kolob, after the heavenly place in their scripture nearest the residence of God. It was a national monument of its own from 1937 until the park took it in, in 1956.

moments.title: Kolob Canyons Visitor Center
moments.text: Everyone stops here to show a park pass or pay the fee. On October 13, 1776, the padres Escalante and Domínguez passed near this spot, the first Europeans known to see the area.

moments.title: Taylor Creek
moments.text: Past a sharp turn the cut face of the Markagunt Plateau opens up with Horse Ranch Mountain, Zion's highest point, above, and the road curves around a box canyon cut by Taylor Creek's south fork.

moments.title: Timber Creek Overlook
moments.text: The road gives out at a turnabout on the ridge, a little above 6,200 feet, looking west to the Kolob Terrace and the Pine Valley Mountains.

practical: The park entrance fee is required even if you are only driving the road, paid at the Kolob Canyons Visitor Center. The road may close in winter for snow or ice.
